entries.mutant: L596 string "a regex shape is searched by the harness's bounded search: none was given" emptied
entries.grounds: At cli_invocation.py:594-596, `_stream_matches` raises TypeError when a `regex` shape is given with no `search`. The mutant empties only the message string (TypeError('')); the exception TYPE is unchanged and the branch is still taken on exactly the same input. The branch is unreachable in production: the only caller that reaches the regex path is `exits_streams` via `verdict_of`, and the `observe` path (cli_invocation.py:1162-1166) always builds a concrete `search` closure over `search_in_worker` and passes it in; the other probes that call `verdict_of` (file_artifact.py:890, python_callable.py:338, python_callable_v2.py:575, process_effect.py:940) never use cls=='exits_streams', so never reach `_stream_matches`'s regex branch. The guard is a programmer-error defense (a caller that forgot the argument). No test pins the message text: tests/v2/test_c2_cli_verdicts.py:238-247 asserts `assertRaises(TypeError)` on the TYPE only (passes with an empty message), and the registered kill file tests/v2/test_v21_r5_regex_worker.py never exercises the `search is None` branch at all (every call supplies a search). No operator/verifier reads the message: _Later.settle (cli_invocation.py:1343-1348) catches only StreamSearchFailed and str()'s that into HARNESS_FAILED detail; a TypeError propagates uncaught (a crash in a buggy caller's traceback), never into a verdict or a report string. Docs (USAGE-2.1.md:628, V2.1-BACKLOG.md V21-68/V21-82) reference `_stream_matches` by line range and structure, not this message. REGISTERED KILL FILE RUN (snapshot 4ec961e, 2026-10-19): tests/v2/test_v21_r5_regex_worker.py PASSES unmutated (OK, 34 tests) and PASSES on the mutant (OK, 34 tests) -> does not kill; survivor confirmed.

exceptions_checked: Owner rule 'a string read by an operator or a verifier is not harmless': checked and does not apply -- this message is a developer diagnostic for a missing-argument programmer error that cannot occur in a real run (observe always supplies search); it is never surfaced to an operator report or a review verifier.

The contract that matters -- 'a regex shape without a search is a TypeError, not an unbounded re.search' -- is the TYPE, pinned by test_c2_cli_verdicts.py; the mutant preserves the type, so that contract still holds.
Not added a test to reach a number: no reader depends on the wording.
